    },

      "title": "Quota guard accepts the forbidden 10% boundary and NaN",

      "file": "docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-uploader/uploader.py",
      "line_start": 19,
      "line_end": 22,
      "confidence": 1,
      "recommendation": "Define quota precision using decimal arithmetic or integer units, reject non-finite shares, and test exact 10%, values on both sides, and NaN."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "title": "Documented bounded memory contradicts eager allocation",
      "body": "The function materializes all records and all batch lists simultaneously. A tracemalloc probe with ten million repeated None records peaked at 162,423,104 bytes, contradicting the docstring's under-4-MB claim even without allocating distinct records. Callers relying on that profile risk memory exhaustion on large uploads.",
      "file": "docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-uploader/uploader.py",
      "line_start": 13,
      "line_end": 14,
      "confidence": 1,
      "recommendation": "Either yield batches incrementally with itertools.islice and measure incremental consumption, or document the actual linear memory profile and remove the false measurement."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "title": "Quota tests never exercise rejection",
      "body": "Both quota tests expect acceptance; neither asserts ValueError. Replacing check_quota_split in memory with an unconditional reserve calculation still passes all five tests, proving that deleting the guard is undetected.",
      "file": "docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-uploader/test_uploader.py",
      "line_start": 18,
      "line_end": 23,
      "confidence": 1,
      "recommendation": "Add assertRaises tests for exactly 10% reserve, less than 10%, and over-allocation, while retaining a valid accepting case."
    }
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Fix the cap and quota validation, correct the memory profile, and rerun tests with boundary and rejecting cases."
  ]
}

result.summary: Do not ship: batches exceed the API cap, the quota boundary is bypassable, and the memory claim is false. All five tests pass despite these defects.

findings.title: Batches exceed the API's 256-record limit
findings.body: make_batches(range(1000)) produces lengths [265, 265, 265, 205]. The first three batches violate the API contract and will be rejected. Existing tests check batch count and total records, which cannot detect this error.
findings.recommendation: Set BATCH_SIZE to 256 and assert every batch respects the literal API cap, including inputs of 256 and 257 records.

findings.title: Quota guard accepts the forbidden 10% boundary and NaN
findings.body: [0.3, 0.3, 0.3] allocates 90%, but floating-point summation produces a reserve of 0.10000000000000009, so the function accepts it. The test explicitly endorses this violation. [float('nan')] also returns NaN because the comparison is false, despite failing to establish a reserve strictly above 10%.
findings.recommendation: Define quota precision using decimal arithmetic or integer units, reject non-finite shares, and test exact 10%, values on both sides, and NaN.

findings.title: Documented bounded memory contradicts eager allocation
findings.body: The function materializes all records and all batch lists simultaneously. A tracemalloc probe with ten million repeated None records peaked at 162,423,104 bytes, contradicting the docstring's under-4-MB claim even without allocating distinct records. Callers relying on that profile risk memory exhaustion on large uploads.
findings.recommendation: Either yield batches incrementally with itertools.islice and measure incremental consumption, or document the actual linear memory profile and remove the false measurement.

findings.title: Quota tests never exercise rejection
findings.body: Both quota tests expect acceptance; neither asserts ValueError. Replacing check_quota_split in memory with an unconditional reserve calculation still passes all five tests, proving that deleting the guard is undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add assertRaises tests for exactly 10% reserve, less than 10%, and over-allocation, while retaining a valid accepting case.

next_steps: Fix the cap and quota validation, correct the memory profile, and rerun tests with boundary and rejecting cases.
